Class Assessment & Examination

Record as many Homework, Class Test and Classwork scores as you need for every student. Each score is entered directly out of the percentage you allocate below (for example, Homework allocated 20% means Homework is marked out of 20). The three parts add up to 100% for the subject. When the examination is included, class assessment counts 30% and the examination 70%.

1. Class assessment percentage allocation

Decide how many marks each part carries. The three must add up to exactly 100%. These marks become the maximum for each column in the score table (e.g. Homework 20 = marked out of 20). When a part has several scores (for example Homework 1, 2, 3), their average is used for that part. Scores already saved are scaled proportionally if you change the percentages.

Tap the words Homework, Class Test or Classwork below to type your own name for each part. It saves automatically.

%
%
%
100%
Class assessment 30%+Examination 70%=Final score 100%

2. Enter scores for a class

Enter each mark out of the maximum shown in the column header. The allocated marks are shared across the columns, so the more columns you add, the smaller each column's maximum becomes (e.g. Homework 20: one column is out of 20, two are out of 10 each, four are out of 5 each). Existing scores are rescaled proportionally when you add or remove a column. Use the + and − buttons to add or remove Homework, Class Test or Classwork columns for this subject. Leave a box empty if that score has not been taken yet. Everything else is calculated automatically.

3. Student PDF reports

The report shows your school logo at the top centre, the school name and location beneath it (from Settings), and the same logo as a faint watermark.

Choose All students in class to produce one PDF with each student on their own page. In the print window choose Save as PDF.

Class Scores

Enter up to five class assessment scores for each student and subject. Each assessment is out of 10; the five scores are added automatically to make the Class Score out of 50. Examination scores are entered on the separate Examination Scores page.

The five assessment scores are saved individually. Their sum is saved as the Class Score / 50 and used by student reports and rankings. Existing examination scores are preserved when you update class assessments.

Examination Scores

Enter the examination mark out of 100 for a student and subject. The app automatically converts it to 50% (out of 50). Class scores are entered on the separate Class Scores page.

Enter the raw examination mark from 1 to 100. The app converts it to a score out of 50 automatically (mark ÷ 2). Reports show the converted /50 score, and existing class scores are preserved.

By class
Expected school fees = fee set for the class (School Supplies page → “School bill / fee”) × number of students in that class, added across classes; a class fee is treated as a per-term amount. Expected feeding fees = the term feeding fee (Settings) for every student in each class. Collected = payments recorded against those bills. Other products (Stationery, Uniform, etc.) = price × quantity entered on the School Supplies page (stock plus units already sold), or amount × students for extra fees; they are counted for all terms. Outstanding = Expected − Collected.

How the daily result is calculated

Net balance = Total money collected − Total recorded expenditure. This is a cash-based daily result from the records available in this app. For a full accounting profit figure, also record stock cost/other business costs as expenditure. Avoid manually entering collections already recorded in the Fees, Feeding Fee, or School Supplies & Bills sections.

How to Use School Bills

  1. Set prices (optional): Open Bill Pricing by Term, choose the term and bill type, enter the standard amount in GHS, then select Save / Update Price.
  2. Add a bill: In School Fees & Other Bills, select the student, bill type and term. Enter a description, amount, any discount or scholarship, and due date, then select Add Bill.
  3. Record money received: Under Record Student Payment, select the term, student and bill. Enter the amount actually received, choose the payment method, add a transaction reference if available, then select Record Payment & Generate Receipt.
  4. Save or print the receipt: In the print dialog, choose Save as PDF or print a paper copy.
  5. Check balances: Review Outstanding by Selected Term, Term Bill Summary, Student Financial Status, and Bills & Payment History.

Important: Adding a bill records what is owed; it does not record a payment. Record only the amount actually received. For a partial payment, enter the partial amount and record any later payment separately.

Debt Page — Students Owing

Search any student by name or ID to check whether they are OWING, PAID, or have NO BILL. This page uses the existing bill and payment records; it does not change them.

Type part of a student’s name or ID (the full name is not needed). If several students match, you will be asked to pick one. Use Save Student Debt as PDF or Print Student Debt for the full statement. Use Save Debt Notice as PDF or Print Debt Notice for Student to produce a student/parent notice showing the outstanding amount and a polite request for payment. For the same colours on computers and other devices, enable “Background graphics” or “Print backgrounds” in the print dialog when available, then choose Save as PDF or your printer.

Choose a term to use its configured date range.

Overpayment / Advance Payment Balance

View each student’s available advance credit or deposit money directly into the student’s credit balance. When the same student later buys school supplies or records a bill in School Supplies & Bills, available credit is applied automatically before calculating the remaining cash payment.

Add Money to Student Advance Credit

Record money received in advance. This adds to the student’s existing credit; it does not mark a specific bill as paid.

Select Refresh balances to load current credit.

Term feeding fee overpayments

Students whose term feeding-fee receipts add up to more than the current term fee (for example after a holiday was added). The extra amount is added to their credit balance above and used automatically on their next payment.

Balances use the existing School Supplies & Bills credit records. Deposits made here are saved to that same credit ledger and can be applied automatically to future bills for the same student.
